clue.text: Specialists in worker management

parts.note: reads like personnel experts handling staff, but the workers are bees and the specialists are beekeepers

explanation.walkthrough: Worker bees are the hive's labour force, so managing workers here means keeping bees.
explanation.definitionFit: Beekeepers tend hives full of worker bees, so they are specialists who manage workers.

clue.text: Countrymen conserving the last British birds

indicators.note: conserving means holding something safe within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: peasants are country people working the land

indicators.note: the last signals taking the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Rural folk preserve the final birds left in Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conserving' puts the final letter of 'British', H, inside PEASANTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pheasants are game birds, common in the British countryside.

clue.text: Tree cared about in Lebanon?

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of cared are moved around

explanation.surface: A tree that is looked after in Lebanon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Lebanon?' points to the famous cedar of Lebanon, the national emblem, and links the definition to its setting.
explanation.definitionFit: A cedar is a large evergreen conifer tree.

clue.text: Several sick rats on sinking ship

indicators.note: sick suggests something in a bad or disordered state, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A number of ill rats aboard a vessel going down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Several sick' looks like it describes the rats, but 'sick' rearranges SEVERAL; rats proverbially desert a sinking ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Rats abandoning a sinking ship are, proverbially, those who depart and desert it.

clue.text: An empty urn will rattle

indicators.note: an empty word has its insides removed, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: will in the sense of resolve or courage, nerve

explanation.surface: An urn with nothing in it will make a rattling noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rattle' looks like the noise the urn makes, but it is the verb meaning to fluster; 'empty' leaves the first and last letters of 'urn', UN.
explanation.definitionFit: To rattle someone is to fluster them and shake their confidence.

clue.text: Hotlines to the Met Office

parts.note: not emergency phone lines but lines on a weather map joining places of equal heat, as drawn by Britain's weather service

explanation.walkthrough: The Met Office is the UK's national weather service.
explanation.definitionFit: Weather maps show lines linking places of the same temperature, so they are lines of heat for forecasters.

clue.text: It's found in bronze giant

indicators.note: found in means placed within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: bronze as a skin colour, a tan
the word it, with 's standing for is

explanation.surface: Something discovered inside a huge bronze statue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bronze' looks like the giant's material, but it means a suntan colour; 'It's found in' reads as it is placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A titan is a person or thing of enormous size or power, after the Greek gods.

clue.text: Writer of illicit love letters?

parts.note: a letter-writer, but with a hyphen added it is the third party in a divorce case for adultery

explanation.walkthrough: In divorce law a co-respondent is the person accused of adultery with the spouse; without the hyphen the word means someone who writes letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who writes letters is one sense; the hyphenated legal sense covers the illicit lover.

clue.text: They keep naughty verses private

indicators.note: naughty means misbehaving, so these letters are put into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone holds on to rude poems in secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naughty' rearranges VERSES and PRIVATE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Preservatives are substances that keep food from spoiling.

clue.text: Maiden could be described in too much detail

parts.note: in cricket a maiden is an over with no runs scored
described as in drawn or depicted

explanation.surface: A young woman who might be portrayed with excessive detail.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over (six balls) bowled without a run conceded; 'could be' links it to OVER.
explanation.definitionFit: An overdrawn account or portrait is exaggerated, given in excess of what is needed.

clue.text: A creature more popular when clipped

indicators.note: clipped means cut short, here losing the first letter

parts.note: hotter means more in demand or fashionable

explanation.surface: An animal becomes better liked once given a trim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when clipped' takes the first letter off HOTTER.
explanation.definitionFit: An otter is a creature, a fish-eating aquatic mammal.

clue.text: A rebel one got out of bed

definitions.meaning: one who rises up in revolt
a ... is someone who gets up, as an early ...

explanation.surface: A rebellious figure who has just got up.
explanation.definitionFit: Rising covers both an uprising and getting up from bed.

clue.text: These receivers used one phrase

indicators.note: used read as worked over, treating the letters as material to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone spoke a single phrase into a handset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' rearranges ONE PHRASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Earphones are receivers worn over or in the ears to hear sound.

clue.text: Origin of neuralgia in Susie's infected cavities

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
infected suggests something corrupted, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken with all its letters, the possessive s included

indicators.note: origin means the beginning, so take the first letter

explanation.surface: Nerve pain that began with Susie's infected sinus cavities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'infected' rearranges SUSIES and 'in' puts N, the first letter of 'neuralgia', inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinuses are air-filled cavities in the bones of the skull.

clue.text: Decoration worn to marches

indicators.note: worn suggests something worn out of shape, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: An ornament that someone wears on parades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worn' looks like a description of the decoration, but it rearranges TO MARCHES. A stomacher was an ornamental panel on the front of an old-fashioned bodice.
explanation.definitionFit: A stomacher is an ornamental, often embroidered panel worn over the chest of a dress.

clue.text: Previously husband of a countess? That's right!

parts.note: a countess is the wife of an earl
that is is abbreviated i.e.

explanation.surface: Was she once married to a nobleman? Quite correct!
explanation.walkthrough: I.e. stands for 'that is', the Latin id est.
explanation.definitionFit: Earlier means at a previous time, before now.

clue.text: Tribesman is chosen to entertain artist

indicators.note: to entertain is to host someone, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: taken as written
the elite are the chosen few
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A tribal member is selected to amuse a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts in London, so crosswords use it for any artist.
explanation.definitionFit: An Israelite was a member of one of the twelve tribes of ancient Israel.

clue.text: Duck and herons flying towards the land

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of zero, shaped like O

indicators.note: flying suggests the letters scatter and come down in a new order

explanation.surface: A duck and some herons fly in from the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' rearranges HERONS to SHORE.
explanation.definitionFit: An onshore wind blows from the sea towards the coast.

clue.text: Plate of select rolls

indicators.note: of here means taken out of, so the letters are drawn from inside these words

explanation.surface: A dish of choice bread rolls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' picks the letters from inside 'select rolls'. Plate is a verb-noun sense: an electrotype or electroplate.
explanation.definitionFit: Electro is short for electroplate or electrotype, a metal plate made by electrolysis.

clue.text: Country inn is a runner here

definitions.text: Country inn is a runner here

parts.words: Country inn is a runner here
parts.note: not a rural pub but the river Inn, which runs through this European nation

explanation.walkthrough: The Inn is a river that flows through the Tyrol on its way to the Danube.
explanation.definitionFit: Austria is a European country through which the Inn flows.

clue.text: A comfort when certain rumours start

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as I left
sure means certain

indicators.note: start signals taking the first letter

explanation.surface: Reassurance comes once gossip begins to look true.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start' takes R from 'rumours'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who assures and reassures others is a source of comfort.

clue.text: Guard seen changing overalls

indicators.note: changing means altering, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sentry is spotted getting changed out of work clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges GUARD SEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Dungarees are hard-wearing overalls with a bib and straps.

clue.text: Take short, naturally

indicators.note: short means cut down, losing a letter

parts.note: to snatch is to take quickly

explanation.surface: Grab a little, of course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the first letter of SNATCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Natch is informal slang meaning of course or as expected.

clue.text: Middle Easterner to dine out after one

indicators.note: after means the rest follows the first piece

parts.note: A is the indefinite article, meaning one

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are out of order

explanation.surface: A man from the Gulf goes out to eat after one o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' gives A, the article meaning one; 'out' signals the rearranged letters of 'dine', placed after it.
explanation.definitionFit: An Adeni is a native of Aden, the port city in Yemen.

clue.text: Writer of comic operas? Not right

indicators.note: comic suggests something played for laughs and jumbled up

explanation.surface: Who wrote humorous operas? Not quite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comic' rearranges OPERAS once R (right) is removed, as 'Not' asks; 'Not right' also says the guess is wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek author of fables.

clue.text: Score from "Concerto for Piano" (Tchaikovsky)

indicators.note: from means taken out of, so the letters are drawn from inside the words

explanation.surface: A piece of music by Tchaikovsky for piano and orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' picks the letters across 'Piano' and 'Tchaikovsky'.
explanation.definitionFit: A notch is a nick cut as a tally mark, so a point or score recorded.

clue.text: Device for letting in single people

definitions.text: Device for letting in single people

parts.words: Device for letting in single people
parts.note: not a dating gadget but a gate admitting one person at a time

explanation.walkthrough: 'single people' suggests the unmarried, but means one person at a time.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotating gate admits people one at a time at entrances.

clue.text: Supplier of programmes for the corps

definitions.text: Supplier of programmes for the corps

parts.words: Supplier of programmes for the corps
parts.note: the corps is the corps de ballet, and the programmes are dance routines rather than printed sheets

explanation.walkthrough: 'Corps' suggests the army, but the corps de ballet is the main body of dancers.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who arranges dance steps provides the routines a ballet company performs.
